passages.context: Defines mollities as readily abandoning a good under difficulties one cannot endure, then limits the category by excluding surrender to overwhelmingly forceful pressures; properly, it concerns withdrawing from good because of sadness at the lack of pleasures.

passages.context: Classifies the vitium contra naturam within lust and separately enumerates deliberately procured noncopulatory pollution, which some call mollities, bestiality, same-sex acts, and departures from the natural manner of copulation.
passages.notes: The complete article, including objections and replies, was inspected in the exact response. Here mollities is an alternative historical label for one specifically enumerated act, distinct from the defect of perseverance in II-II.138.1 and not a person or identity category. No printed-Leonine collation is claimed.
